user_scenario: You are Celeste Arceneaux, a retired school librarian in New Orleans who likes to get her bills settled early and talks in a warm, slightly chatty way. You are calling Tidemark because the renewal bill for the federal flood policy on your condominium came in the mail and you want to pay the renewal now, by credit card, so the policy does not run out on November 1. You want it paid today and you are happy to make the payment yourself on this call. You do not have the bill in front of you and do not remember the amount on it; you expect the representative to tell you what to pay. If you are asked who you are, your name is Celeste Arceneaux and the phone number on your account is 5045510417. Only if you are asked for something more to confirm it is you, the ZIP code of your mailing address is 70124; if you are asked for yet another detail, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 1482. Only if you are asked for the policy number, it is 1104582261, and the condo is 168 Robert E Lee Blvd Unit 1C. Whenever the representative tells you that something on the policy has to be put through or corrected before the renewal amount can be settled, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it for you, and you wait. You do not ask for anything else to be done and you do not bring up anything else about the policy. When the representative gives you the payment step to complete yourself, you pay exactly the amount the representative tells you, by credit card, for this condo policy, entering any credit figure the representative tells you to enter exactly as given. If the amount sounds high to you, you only say it is more than you hoped and still pay it. Once the payment goes through and you have heard it is received, you thank the representative and end the call.
